I need to identify the molecular formula of a compound in a sample. The only tool available is mass spectrometry with ESI (Electrospray Ionization) technique. 

Mass spectrometry will give me mass-to-charge (m/z) ratios of ions, which can help determine the molecular weight of the compound. From the molecular weight and the fragmentation pattern, I can deduce the molecular formula.

<thought>
The mass spectrometry data shows:
- Base peak (100% intensity) at m/z 183.0450916283
- Isotope peak at m/z 184.048 (10.25% intensity) - this is the M+1 peak
- Significant peak at m/z 185.042 (32.67% intensity) - this is the M+2 peak

The M+2 peak at ~33% intensity is characteristic of chlorine (Cl has two isotopes: 35Cl at 75.8% and 37Cl at 24.2%, giving an M+2 peak at about 1/3 of the base peak for one Cl atom).

The base peak at m/z 183.045 likely represents [M+H]+ or [M-H]- depending on ionization mode. Given ESI typically produces [M+H]+ in positive mode, the molecular weight is likely 182.

Let me analyze the molecular formula:
- Molecular weight ≈ 182
- Contains at least one Cl (based on M+2 isotope pattern)
- m/z 183.045 suggests the exact mass

For a compound with Cl:
- If we have C, H, O, and Cl
- Cl has mass ~35 (for 35Cl)
- Remaining mass: 182 - 35 = 147

Looking at common formulas with Cl:
- C8H7O2Cl would have mass: 8(12) + 7(1) + 2(16) + 35 = 96 + 7 + 32 + 35 = 170 (too low)
- C9H7O2Cl would have mass: 9(12) + 7(1) + 2(16) + 35 = 108 + 7 + 32 + 35 = 182 ✓

Let me verify with exact mass:
C9H7O2Cl: 9(12.000) + 7(1.00783) + 2(15.9994) + 34.9689 = 108 + 7.055 + 31.999 + 34.969 = 182.023

The observed m/z of 183.045 would be [M+H]+ = 182.023 + 1.008 = 183.031

This is close but let me reconsider. The exact mass 183.0450916283 for [M+H]+ means M = 182.037.

Actually, looking more carefully at the isotope pattern with M+2 at 32.67%, this strongly indicates one chlorine atom.

C9H7O2Cl has exact mass: 182.0134 (using exact masses)
[M+H]+ would be 183.0212

8(12) + 8(1) + 3(16) + 35 = 96 + 8 + 48 + 35 = 187 (too high)

C9H7ClO2 seems most likely with mass 182.
</thought>
